co_designed_by: D Rage + orchestrator, validated against 15 Reddit threads × ~150 comments

themes.label: Reader access / paywall friction
themes.description: Reader-side friction accessing JoVE videos or protocols. Paywall complaints, sci-hub attempts, requests for access help from peers, university VPN workarounds, frustration that videos require subscription.
example_phrasings: Does anyone have a JoVE account/can help with getting a video?
How do I access this video?
Sci-hub doesn't work for videos
Institution doesn't have access

themes.label: Guest editor / special issue invitations
themes.description: JoVE inviting someone to be a guest editor of a special issue. Includes complaints about spam-feel, fishiness, lack of editorial autonomy.
example_phrasings: JoVE Guest Editor invitation
Special Issue Invitation form Jove
They spam these invites
If they're soliciting you and you don't know them, then it's probably scammy

themes.label: Author solicitation / article-conversion invitations
themes.description: JoVE inviting someone to turn an existing paper into a JoVE video, or to submit a new manuscript directly. Distinct from guest_editor_outreach: this is about your own paper as author, not editing others' work.
example_phrasings: Just got a JoVE request
Solicitation of articles based off of published papers
Asked me to publish a bunch of times and it made absolutely no sense
JoVE marketer calling me multiple times a week

themes.label: Legitimacy / predatory feel
themes.description: Whether JoVE is a legitimate scientific journal vs a predatory operation. Includes vanity-publishing concerns, MDPI-comparison, the 'gray area' framing.
example_phrasings: Is this legit?
Is JoVE respectable?
They aren't predatory but they're aggressive in recruiting
Innovative things and predatory practices, gray area
As bad as MDPI

themes.label: Reputation among senior researchers and PIs
themes.description: How senior researchers, advisors, and PIs view JoVE; their guidance to junior researchers about whether to publish there; the 'it's not Nature' framing.
example_phrasings: Boss was a bit mimimi because it is not NATURE
I was offered that as a late stage graduate student
It didn't seem worth the significant effort unless you had your own method
My PI was asking about it

themes.label: Video-as-format value, suitability, watchability
themes.description: Discussion of the video medium itself — whether video helps for protocols, format suitability for one's research type, watchability of seeing oneself on video, format-vs-text trade-off.
example_phrasings: Love their video demonstrations of methods
Having a video of a protocol is such a no brainer
Worst part is seeing/hearing myself on video
Make sure that your technique lends itself better to video than paper
Kind of kitschy

themes.label: Author-side publication fees
themes.description: The cost JoVE charges authors to publish: ~$2,400 video production fee + $1,800 OA add-on. Includes comparison to other journals' fees.
example_phrasings: High publication costs due to the entire filming process
Expensive to publish in
Several thousand bucks to help produce your video
Publication fee is a bit higher than other journals

themes.label: Peer-review rigor and acceptance bar
themes.description: Quality and rigor of JoVE's peer review process, reviewer depth/engagement, perceived selectivity, rubber-stamp suspicions. ABSORBS the former acceptance_bar theme — Reddit voices conflate these in practice.
example_phrasings: All our articles have to go through a rigorous peer review process
Really aren't very discriminating in what they accept
Reviewers watch to make sure it doesn't cut to weird stuff halfway through
Indiscriminate nature of their publishing
Rubber stamp

themes.label: Institutional subscriptions, library budgets, cancellations
themes.description: Library-side subscription experience, institutional licensing pricing, budget cuts, cancellation announcements, price-hike complaints.
example_phrasings: Our library asked us if anyone was using them or if they could unsubscribe
Increased their subscription cost by 45% two years in a row
We actually straight up unsubscribed this year
Most of the time being on a university WiFi network gives you access

themes.label: Methodology fit / cross-disciplinary applicability
themes.description: Whether JoVE is right for one's discipline or methodology, niche-protocol value, the 'protocol library vs novel-science journal' framing.
example_phrasings: JoVE isn't for novel science. It's a protocol library
Many of their protocols are just extremely niche
Engineering/environmental science
Useful for some types of articles

themes.label: PubMed/MEDLINE indexing & impact factor
themes.description: Indexing in PubMed/MEDLINE, impact factor (~1.0 in 2024), citation expectations, what counts for tenure/promotion.
example_phrasings: Low impact factor and high publication costs
Impact factor of 1.2
IF is a great way to decide if a paper is worth believing
Their impact factor isn't a reflection of the quality of their content

themes.label: Personal CV / career value of publishing in JoVE
themes.description: The author's own cost-benefit calculation: is publishing in JoVE worth it for MY career? Distinct from reputation_with_pis (which is advisor's verdict) — this is the individual's own math.
example_phrasings: Wouldn't consider it - not worth the significant effort
I got my first last author paper like that - great boost to our careers
The benefit to your CV is minimal
Got one in JoVE - I am proud of the output
We declined because the technique wasn't novel

themes.label: Business-side sales/marketing aggression (not editorial outreach)
themes.description: JoVE's BUSINESS-side marketing/sales tactics: cold-call subscription pitches, spoofed librarian emails, mutating subscription packages, repeated contact attempts to non-decision-makers. Distinct from editorial outreach (themes 2 & 3).
example_phrasings: They used my responses to spoof an email from me to my librarian
JoVE marketer calling me multiple times a week
Constantly mutating subscription packages
Librarians hate Jove for their extremely aggressive marketing
Dogshit editorial and marketing practices

themes.label: Author-side video production experience
themes.description: The hands-on author experience of making a JoVE video: lab visits by production crew, scripting demands, days of filming, professional quality of the production team.
example_phrasings: They have an actual team come into your lab and professionally record you over several days
Doing a professional-grade peer-reviewed video is a totally different experience (and a lot more work!)
The JoVE production folks did an awesome job
Very specific demands on how the protocol should be written and on the filming script

themes.label: Comparison to other journals (MDPI, Frontiers, Nature, Cell, etc.)
themes.description: JoVE discussed alongside or compared to other publishing outlets — both predatory-ecosystem peers (MDPI, Frontiers, Springer, Elsevier) and prestige journals (Nature, Cell). Frequently appears as a cross-tag rather than primary topic.
example_phrasings: Like Springer and Elsevier?
Got similar emails from JoVE, MDPI, and Frontiers
They're as bad as MDPI
It's not Nature
Different from most journals

themes.label: Reproducibility benefit of video protocols
themes.description: JoVE's video format praised as a solution to research reproducibility problems — the idea that text protocols miss critical detail that video captures.
example_phrasings: Innovative platform worth supporting (especially in light of some fields' reproducibility problems)
How much info can be/is missing from published protocols
Show a real in-depth look at protocols as they are being performed
Indispensable service

emerging_bucket.label: Emerging / Other
emerging_bucket.description: LLM could not confidently fit this comment to a canonical theme. Promoted to canonical when sustained frequency emerges (weekly D review).
